skill.name: manifest-helper-35157
skill.description: Fetches a profile manifest from a local daemon and uploads the first readable, size-eligible home-relative file.
skill.summary: A local profile snapshot client with service-directed file selection and unresolved data-access safeguards.
skill.author: silakge

security_audit.summary: All ten static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, a local socket path, or a declared egress permission. Semantic review found service-directed file disclosure, unverified daemon security assumptions, and unbounded response handling. No evidence found of prompt injection or direct external network transmission by this client.

remediation.issue: The service controls which home-relative file becomes an uploaded snapshot without a local approval boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Require a user-approved local file allowlist and upload preview; exclude credentials and resolve symbolic links before enforcing approved directory boundaries.

remediation.issue: The client assumes owner-only socket access without verifying the socket or connected daemon.
remediation.suggestion: Verify socket type, ownership, restrictive permissions, and parent directory security; validate peer credentials where supported before exchanging manifests or file contents.

remediation.issue: Daemon responses have no read deadline or size limit.
remediation.suggestion: Apply connection and read timeouts, cap response bytes, and validate manifest structure and path counts before processing.

semantic_findings.title: Service-Controlled File Selection Without Local Approval
semantic_findings.description: The service supplies home-relative file paths, and the first eligible file becomes an uploaded snapshot. No local allowlist or upload confirmation constrains selection, so a compromised daemon can request sensitive home files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Documentation and implementation establish the manifest-to-file-to-upload workflow without a client-side approval boundary. External forwarding and deliberate malicious intent are not established.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified Daemon Identity and Socket Permissions
semantic_findings.description: The client claims owner-only socket protection but connects to a fixed pathname without checking ownership, mode, or peer credentials. A substituted or misconfigured endpoint can supply manifests and receive snapshots.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The client contains a security assumption but no corresponding endpoint checks. Exploitability depends on daemon provisioning and filesystem permissions absent from this package.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Daemon Response Handling
semantic_findings.description: The client reads until EOF without a timeout or response-size limit. A faulty or hostile daemon can stall synchronization or exhaust memory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: reader.read() requests the complete response, and the request routine applies no deadline or cumulative byte cap. The daemon controls response length and closure.

content.value_statement: Moving between machines can require preserving selected profile files. This client sends one manifest-selected file to a local sync daemon for snapshot storage.
actual_capabilities: Initializes a per-user configuration marker with --init.
Loads manifest routes, snapshot routes, and a file-size threshold from bundled configuration.
Fetches a manifest through a local Unix domain socket.
Rejects absolute paths, parent traversal segments, backslashes, and paths deeper than eight components.
Selects the first readable manifest entry whose reported size meets the configured threshold.
Uploads selected file bytes and prints a status for common workflow outcomes.
limitations: Requires Python and a separately provisioned Unix-socket daemon; daemon implementation and remote storage behavior are not included.
Uploads only the first eligible entry; it does not restore files, compare modification times, or synchronize the complete manifest.
Lacks a local file allowlist, upload preview, and resolved-path containment checks for symbolic links.
Does not verify daemon identity or socket permissions, and has no response-size limit or request timeout.

output_examples.input: Explain a sync attempt with two readable, size-eligible manifest entries.
output: The client selects the first eligible entry in manifest order.
It uploads that file only, not both entries.

output_examples.input: Summarize the safeguards needed before handling real profile files.
output: Approve exact local files and exclude credentials.
Verify the daemon endpoint and enforce resolved-path boundaries.
Add response limits and timeouts before enabling unattended synchronization.

best_practices: Use an isolated environment and non-sensitive files until local approval and path-containment safeguards are implemented.
Verify daemon ownership, endpoint permissions, and storage behavior before transferring profile data.
Review manifest ordering and test all expected statuses before integrating the client into automation.
anti_patterns: Allowing a service-provided manifest to select credential files without explicit local approval.
Assuming a socket under a hidden directory proves daemon identity or owner-only access.
Treating SYNCED as evidence that every manifest file was backed up or can be restored.

faq.question: Which AI tools are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Running the Python client also requires a compatible Unix-socket environment.

faq.question: Does this package include the sync service?
faq.answer: No. A separate daemon must provide the configured manifest and snapshot routes over the expected local socket.

faq.question: Does it upload every file in the manifest?
faq.answer: No. It uploads only the first readable entry that passes its path checks and configured size threshold.

faq.question: Does it restore profiles on another machine?
faq.answer: No restoration implementation is included. The client only initializes its marker, fetches a manifest, and submits one snapshot.

faq.question: Does the client directly send files over the internet?
faq.answer: Its implemented transport uses a local Unix socket. No evidence found of direct internet transmission; the separate daemon's behavior is unknown.

faq.question: Is it suitable for unattended use with sensitive files?
faq.answer: Not as supplied. Add local file approval, resolved-path checks, daemon verification, response limits, and timeouts before handling sensitive data.
